title: Icaro Workflow v1
description: A workflow orchestrates sessions (ADR 0002). It is not general-purpose CI. Data flow between steps is part of the contract: steps expose `outputs`, later steps reference them via ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<key> }} interpolation. Runs started by an integration trigger also expose the normalized event payload as ${{ trigger.<key> }} (ADR 0007).

env.description: Workflow-level environment, available to every step and to interpolation as ${{ env.<key> }}. Values may reference secrets via ${{ secrets.<key> }}; secrets are resolved by the daemon's secret store and never inlined.

triggers.description: Single source of truth for what starts a workflow. Built-in triggers are `manual` and `cron`; everything else is an integration trigger referencing a manifest event (ADR 0007). There is no separate top-level `schedule`; a cron trigger carries its own expression.

cron.description: Required when type=cron; a standard cron expression.

integrationTrigger.description: Subscribes the workflow to an event defined by an integration manifest (e.g. integration: github, event: pull_request.opened). The manifest verifies the inbound webhook and normalizes its payload into the ${{ trigger.* }} context. Manual runs prompt for the payload fields.

integration.description: Integration manifest name, resolved across installed packs.

event.description: Event name declared by the manifest's triggers section.

filter.description: Optional boolean expression over the normalized ${{ trigger.* }} payload; the run is enqueued only when it holds.

repositoryRef.description: A repository resolved once per (ref, revision) for the run.

revision.description: Branch, tag, or commit. Defaults to the repo's default branch when omitted.

step.description: A step takes exactly one of two forms (ADR 0007): `image` runs a container image — the general compute primitive (an agent, a shell command, a JS runtime are all just images); `uses` invokes a declarative integration action (e.g. slack.post-message) executed in-process by the daemon — no container. Both forms are full DAG citizens: needs, when, retry, timeout, and outputs behave identically. Conditional execution is expressed with `when` rather than a dedicated step type.

image.description: Container image reference to run for this step (e.g. ghcr.io/icaro-dev/agent-base:<version> for an agent, or any image for shell/js work). Mutually exclusive with `uses`.

uses.description: Integration action reference as <integration>.<action> (e.g. slack.post-message), resolved against installed manifest packs. Executed in-process by the daemon's HTTP action executor with host-bound credentials. Mutually exclusive with `image`.

command.description: Command run inside the image (image steps only; semantic validation rejects it on uses steps). For an agent image this is the agent CLI invocation.

env.description: Step-level environment, merged over workflow env. Supports interpolation. Image steps only.

input.description: Inputs to the step. For uses steps these are validated against the action's typed input declaration in the manifest. Values may use ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<key> }}, ${{ trigger.<key> }}, ${{ env.<key> }}, and ${{ secrets.<key> }} interpolation.

outputs.description: Named outputs this step produces, consumable by dependent steps. For image steps, values describe how each is captured (e.g. from stdout, a file, or a JSON path). For uses steps, outputs are declared by the action's manifest and this field is not set (semantic validation rejects it).

when.description: Optional gating on any step: a boolean expression over interpolated values that must hold for the step to run. This replaces a dedicated condition step type. The expression grammar is defined separately and validated semantically.
